The final version came back with the annual cap and one and a half per cent, which is exactly what we asked for, and the finance director noticed. Second, and this is the reason I am calling. It is a concession agreement with the state, it runs for thirty years, and the whole value of the project depends on carbon credits that a certification body still has to approve. Nobody here has done this before, including me. I have sent you the framework document. Read the first ten pages and tell me on Monday what worries you most. Thank you, Amanda.

Good morning, everyone, and welcome to the opening session. Before the technical part, a short introduction for those of you who are new to this market. A carbon credit is a unit. One credit is one tonne of carbon dioxide that was not released into the atmosphere, or that was taken out of it. Somebody has to certify that the tonne is real, and that is the job of an independent verification body. The activity behind the credit can be many things, but in this region it is usually reforestation, because the land is there and the trees do the work. The legal part matters more than people expect. Most of these projects sit on a concession agreement with the state, which means that for the next thirty years two parties have to keep a promise about the same piece of land. Every lawyer in this room knows what that means.

Say who you are and what your team handles. Then say how long you have been there and where you started. Then say what you have been working on this month. Then say what will happen if the current project goes through. And finally, say what would happen if it did not, and what you would do about it.
